metadata.note: The Dayton and Michigan Railroad's own era, 1853-1863: Dayton - Toledo drawn as five sections, each from its own opening year to the 1 May 1863 perpetual lease to the Cincinnati, Hamilton and Dayton. Non-overlapping sections so the line grows north year by year without double drawing. The D&M owned one line and no branches (ICC Val. vol. 42: 139.966 mi, all built by the company); it never built in Michigan.
metadata.ownership_split: D&M to 1863 here; CH&D 1863-1917 and B&O 1917-1971 already drawn on identical geometry in cincinnati_hamilton_and_dayton_railway.geojson.
conflicts: Piqua opening: 1854 (Ohio Commissioner 1867) vs 1856 (Harbaugh 1909); drawn from 1856.
Operator 1859-1863: ICC Val. vol. 42 says CH&D from 1859; contemporary D&M timetables signed by the D&M superintendent say D&M. Drawn as D&M to the 1863 lease.
Toledo completion day: 28 Jul (michiganrailroads.com), 18 Aug last rail (Perrysburg Journal), 1 Sep opening (Ohio Commissioner 1867) - same year, no effect on drawn span.
not_yet_sourced: Whether Sidney - Wapakoneta opened before Lima (1857?).
D&M running times and frequency outside Nov 1858; avg_speed_kmh and headway_min are estimates.
omitted: Piqua and Troy Branch RR (1883, CH&D-operated, not D&M property).
Wapakoneta - St. Marys connection: a road hack, not rail (Rule 5 would exclude it anyway).
Through routes to Chicago (PFW&C), Detroit (Michigan Southern side) and Cincinnati (CH&D) - other companies' track.
metadata.freight_only_check: Nothing excluded: one line, carried passengers from each opening.
metadata.colour: #8A4F7D new for Dayton and Michigan Railroad; checked unused in data/ (distinct from CH&D #E07B39 and B&O #00447C).

segments.note: Dayton - Troy, the first stage of the D&M, "opened for traffic, from Dayton to Troy, in April, 1853" (Ohio Commissioner of Railroads and Telegraphs, Annual Report for 1867, which calls the stations "for receiving passengers and freight"). Steam from opening; no animal-power era. Ends at the perpetual lease of the D&M to the Cincinnati, Hamilton and Dayton on 1 May 1863 (Ohio Commissioner of Railroads, Annual Report for 1873); from 1863 the same track is drawn as chd-dayton-toledo (CH&D 1863-1917) and bo-dayton-toledo (B&O 1917-1971). CONFLICT: ICC Valuation vol. 42 says the CH&D operated the D&M from its completion in 1859; contemporary D&M timetables (Nov 1858, Apr 1859, Nov 1862, Feb 1863) were signed by the D&M's own superintendent R. M. Shoemaker beside separately signed CH&D ads, so this feature follows the 1863 lease. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE from the D&M's Nov 1858 "Two Daily Trains" advertisement (Dayton Daily Empire, 6 Apr 1859); no frequency is sourced for other years.
sources: Segment-level: April 1853 opening from Ohio Commissioner of Railroads and Telegraphs, Annual Report for 1867; 1 May 1863 lease from the same, Annual Report for 1873 (both read for research/branches/dayton_and_michigan_railroad.txt, 2026-10-29)

segments.note: Sidney - Wapakoneta - Lima. Start 1858 from positive passenger evidence: a D&M timetable "ON AND AFTER MONDAY, NOV. 29, 1858, Passenger trains will leave Dayton ... for Sidney, Lima", connecting at Lima with the Pittsburgh, Fort Wayne & Chicago (Dayton Daily Empire, 6 Apr 1859 p.4); Ohio Historical Marker 5-6 at Wapakoneta also gives 1858. Whether Sidney - Wapakoneta opened earlier (e.g. 1857) is not established, so nothing earlier is drawn. Ends at the perpetual lease of the D&M to the Cincinnati, Hamilton and Dayton on 1 May 1863 (Ohio Commissioner of Railroads, Annual Report for 1873); from 1863 the same track is drawn as chd-dayton-toledo (CH&D 1863-1917) and bo-dayton-toledo (B&O 1917-1971). CONFLICT: ICC Valuation vol. 42 says the CH&D operated the D&M from its completion in 1859; contemporary D&M timetables (Nov 1858, Apr 1859, Nov 1862, Feb 1863) were signed by the D&M's own superintendent R. M. Shoemaker beside separately signed CH&D ads, so this feature follows the 1863 lease. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE from the D&M's Nov 1858 "Two Daily Trains" advertisement (Dayton Daily Empire, 6 Apr 1859); no frequency is sourced for other years.

segments.note: Lima - Ottawa - Deshler - Perrysburg - Toledo, built from both ends in 1859. Last rail laid near Ottawa on 18 Aug 1859 (Perrysburg Journal, 25 Aug 1859); opened to Toledo 1 Sept 1859 (Ohio Commissioner 1867). D&M trains crossed the Maumee on the Cleveland and Toledo's bridge into Toledo (Ohio Commissioner 1873). By 1862-63 the D&M advertised a "Toledo and Chicago Mail" and a "Chicago and Detroit Express". Ends at the perpetual lease of the D&M to the Cincinnati, Hamilton and Dayton on 1 May 1863 (Ohio Commissioner of Railroads, Annual Report for 1873); from 1863 the same track is drawn as chd-dayton-toledo (CH&D 1863-1917) and bo-dayton-toledo (B&O 1917-1971). CONFLICT: ICC Valuation vol. 42 says the CH&D operated the D&M from its completion in 1859; contemporary D&M timetables (Nov 1858, Apr 1859, Nov 1862, Feb 1863) were signed by the D&M's own superintendent R. M. Shoemaker beside separately signed CH&D ads, so this feature follows the 1863 lease. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE from the D&M's Nov 1858 "Two Daily Trains" advertisement (Dayton Daily Empire, 6 Apr 1859); no frequency is sourced for other years.
